title: The Rise of the AI Software Engineer: Jesse Han
talk_summary: This is a short product announcement from Morph Labs for a 'code index' — a neurosymbolic code database combining static analysis, vector embeddings, and graph algorithms for semantic code search, plus a pipeline to turn an indexed codebase into training data for a small code-editing model (Rift Coder 7B). It is mostly marketing; the only transferable mechanisms are retrieval-based codebase context and codebase-derived training data.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid static-analysis + embedding + graph code index for retrieval
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a code search index using static analysis, vector embeddings, and graph algorithms, exposed via a query language, so a coding assistant can retrieve codebase-wide context instead of stuffing files into the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We use static analysis vector embeddings and graph algorithms to create a state-of-the-art code search index

takeaways.technique: Neurosymbolic query language for precise lookups
takeaways.what_they_do: Pair fuzzy semantic search with a structured query language so results can be guaranteed precise (e.g. exact symbol/reference queries) rather than only approximate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a Naros symbolic query language which can be used to guarantee precise results

takeaways.technique: Generate training data from your own indexed codebase
takeaways.what_they_do: Traverse the indexed codebase with a generation script to produce training examples, then fine-tune a small code-editing model on them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all you have to do is index your code run the generation script and you can start training your personal AI software engineer
takeaways.numbers: Rift Coder 7B described as an open-source code-editing model that runs on a laptop/IDE
